title: Signed indexing of a Boolean list
statement: Let $x$ be a finite Boolean string and let $b : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ agree with $x$, so that $b(j)=x_j$ whenever $j<|x|$. For every $s\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ and $j\in\mathbb{N}$, the following holds: if $s$ is true and $j>0$, both sides are undefined; otherwise, the expression that returns $b(j)$ when $s$ is false and $j<|x|$, or when $s$ is true and $j=0<|x|$, and is undefined in all other cases, equals the partial lookup of $x$ at the integer position $1-j$ when $s$ is true and $1+j$ when $s$ is false.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean sequence b agreeing with x at every index below the length of x
